blocks.content: Repo rate is the key benchmark interest rate at which the Reserve Bank of India lends short-term funds to commercial banks.

rows: Rate at which RBI lends money to commercial banks
Rate at which RBI borrows money/absorbs liquidity from banks
Used to control inflation and supply liquidity
Used to control excess money supply in the banking system
Always higher than Reverse Repo Rate
Commercial banks pledge government securities to RBI
RBI transfers government securities to commercial banks

items: Questions frequently test the core difference: RBI lends at Repo Rate, whereas banks park funds with RBI at Reverse Repo Rate.
Remember that Primary Deficit = Fiscal Deficit - Interest Payments (a recurring direct formula question in SSC CGL and UPSC).
Stagflation contradicts the traditional Phillips Curve relationship and is a favorite concept in competitive economics papers.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Repo Rate is the rate at which the Reserve Bank of India lends short-term funds to commercial banks against government securities.
Reverse Repo Rate is the rate at which the RBI absorbs excess liquidity from commercial banks.
Stagflation refers to a situation of high inflation occurring simultaneously with stagnant economic growth and high unemployment.
Primary Deficit is derived by subtracting interest payments from the overall Fiscal Deficit.
